However, for arbitrary pairs $(a, b) \in S^2$, the sum $a + b$ can be as large as $142 + 142 = 284$. In fact, by the bijection $(a, b) \mapsto (143 - a, 143 - b)$, exactly half of the pairs in $S^2$ with $a + b \neq 143$ satisfy $a + b < 143$. Thus, at most $\frac{120^2}{2} = 7200$ pairs in $S^2$ have $a + b < 143$. 

The proposed solution completely ignores the condition $a + b < 143$, leading to an impossible answer of $11760$, which exceeds the upper bound of $7200$.
